newsitem.title: UK: Amstrad ups provisions as losses narrow.
newsitem.headline: Amstrad ups provisions as losses narrow.

text.p: British electronics group Amstrad Plc reported reduced first half losses on Tuesday, but warned it would need to set aside more cash for restructuring its Amstrad Consumer Electronics, once its core business.
The firm's pretax loss in the six months to December 31 1996 fell to 1.78 million pounds ($2.91 million) from 5.40 million the previous year. Sales fell to 154.05 million pounds from 162.05 million.
The dividend was held at 1.25 pence a share.
Chairman Alan Sugar said rationalising ACE had taken longer than expected and a further 6.4 million pounds would be provided for the restructuring in the current finacial year.
"Completion of the ACE restructuring will focus the group firmly on the technology businesses of Dancall and Viglen and entry into the digital set top box market," he said in a statement.
Sugar, the entrepreneur who founded the business, said the risks of more losses from the rationalising ACE depended on whether there was any further product price erosion.

Amstrad became a stock market high flier in the 1980s on the back of Sugar's success in selling personal computers to the masses. But its star faded when its computers started losing ground to competitors in the United States and Japan.
ACE's losses became a drain on the group and prompted the restructuring, which began last year.
The mobile phone business Dancall boosted sales to 45.5 million pounds from 38.1 million and made a profit in the last quarter of the first half.

Viglen's operating profit was flat at 4.7 million pounds, while sale fell to 47.5 million from 50.8 million. Sugar said Viglen had done well to maintain its profits when selling prices had been falling.

Betacom, whose results show the impact of ACE UK's activities for the first time, increased operating profit to 1.3 million pounds form 200,000, while sales increased to 24.9 million from 6.9 million.
Last year Betacom took on ACE's activities in audio, video, television and facsimile products as part of the restructuring process.

Amstrad had 112.4 million pounds net cash at the end of December, up from 91.2 million at the same stage in 1995. Sugar said this reflected a reduction of stocks from ACE and Dancall and a further payment relating to the purchase of Viglen.
"We continue to examine options to return value to shareholders," he said.
Amstrad's shares rose 2-1/2 pence to 166-1/2. ($1=.6120 Pound)
